snapshot_note: v0.54.0 released on develop 2026-07-27 — six C++ correctness fixes, four of them SILENT wrong answers, all found by following one reducer down. A qualified name in an OPERAND position was returned bare instead of continuing its postfix chain, so every ( [ . -> after it was dropped and re-read by the caller as a fresh expression: (int)N::f(x) silently became (int)(x) and --emit=c11 printed `return "abc";`, while (int)N::arr[1] sent the orphaned [ to the LAMBDA-introducer dispatch. Under that sat (int)S::f(4) reporting "undeclared identifier 'S'" — the shape every string header is built from — where the operand path carried a narrow COPY of the class-qualifier rule that the shared resolver (four other callers) already owned. Under THAT, a static data member read as 0 from inside its own class body where g++ gives 42: storage was registered only by the out-of-class definition, which is parsed after member-function bodies. g++'s model transferred exactly (finish_static_data_member_decl creates the decl in the class body; the definition COMPLETES that decl) and madc's DECL_IN_AGGR_P turned out to be vfEXTERN, whose completion addVariable already implemented — nothing new was invented. Also: a nested type is now a member of its enclosing scope with `struct` spelled too, earning class-hood alongside an object member and an NSDMI on the principle the promotion site already stated (the keyword does not decide struct-vs-class, the contents do). TWO OF THREE BATTERIES ON THE STATIC-MEMBER FIX WENT RED and 45 green reducers said nothing about either — the suite found what the reducers structurally could not. Shipped with two labelled placeholders: system-header class statics still fold (no Itanium storage_alias_name for class statics yet — itanium_mangle_nested_var already takes an arbitrary qualifier chain, so it is within reach), and two scopes each declaring `struct Inner` still collide. Two controls killed it: a function DEFINED in a namespace, with no using-declaration anywhere, failed IDENTICALLY; and a global `using ::wcslen;` called UNQUALIFIED was correct. The shared factor was a QUALIFIED NAME IN AN OPERAND POSITION. The wcslen reducer was just the first form I happened to write, and its most distinctive feature (the using-declaration) was the one thing that did not matter. LESSON: a reducer with an unnecessary ingredient names the wrong layer; run ONE control with the suspect REMOVED before believing it. KG node corrected to superseded, not deleted.

ROOT CAUSE (fixed @6476c8ea): parsePostfixChain resolves an identifier head and then continues the postfix chain at its tail — parsePostfixChainFrom(result, postfix_expr_variable(result)). Its QUALIFIED arms did not; they returned the resolved value bare. So every `(`, `[`, `.`, `->` after a qualified name in an OPERAND position was dropped and re-read by the caller as a fresh expression:
  (int)N::f(x)         SILENT, became (int)(x) — the ARGUMENT was the value. --emit=c11 printed `return "abc";`
  (int)N::arr[1]       "Expecting ] in lambda expression" — the orphaned `[` reached the LAMBDA-introducer dispatch
  (int)N::s.b          "member reference is not a structure or union"
  int v = (int)N::f(x) "lvalue required as left operand of assignment"
Not cast-only: parsePostfixChain is equally the deref / address-of / complex-component operand path. `(` also needed its own arm — it IS a postfix operator, but an unqualified `f(x)` cast operand is claimed earlier by parse_cast_function_call_operand, so the hole only opened once a qualifier put the head on a path that reaches the chain. Chaining and overloads (N::mk(4).b, N::slot(1)[1], N::pick(1) vs N::pick("a")) came free — always correct, never reached.

SECOND FIX @522803c7: (int)S::f(4) said "undeclared identifier 'S'" — the shape every string header is built from, (size_t)char_traits<char>::length(p). The operand path carried a narrow COPY of the class-qualifier rule: it probed for a static DATA member and handed every other shape to "the existing paths below", which were findVariable("S"). Adopted resolve_class_qualified_expression, the shared owner with four other callers (nested scopes, operator-ids, explicit template args, access control, dependent surfaces). The call is built at the call site, not by the chain's generic `(` arm, because ResolvedFunction deliberately leaves the `(` to the caller so reselect_static_member_overload can run once arg types are known.

Reducers: tmp/udecl/r35,r36,r37 (0, wrong) vs r38,r39,r40 (correct).
